title: ZTIE correlation-result (Nova Pro static↔dynamic correlation) contract (v1)
description: The bounded, DERIVED, verdict-free correlation result produced by the Story 3.2 Hub-side Nova Pro correlation engine (RD-035) for one intake artifact — the AI-correlation core of Phase 3 (Correlation & Synthesis). It hands the ONE normalized combined-event record (Story 3.1, RD-033) for an intake_id to Amazon Nova Pro (RD-003, via bedrock-runtime, with exponential-backoff retry on throttling/5xx), correlates the static misconfigurations with the dynamic behavioral indicators, and records the result back onto the SAME Hub tracking item. It is NOT a Forensic -> Hub crossing (its input already lives Hub-side); it is a Hub-INTERNAL derived field written by the 3.2 correlator Lambda, so it carries NO gate discriminator. It reasons ONLY over 3.1's bounded combined event and references nothing raw (RD-009): no raw body, findings text, command log or raw trace. It records the invocation HONESTLY — a 'status' (correlated / model_error / unparseable / skipped_no_signals), the model id, the number of Bedrock attempts (so the retry is inspectable), and whether output was truncated — so a model failure is never hidden behind a fabricated correlation. It is NOT a verdict: there is NO verdict/safe/approved/forward/pass_fail/malicious/clean field anywhere and the prompt never asks the model for one; 'severity' roll-ups describe EVIDENCE and the verdict is Hub-side/human-gated (Phase 4). Allow-list: additionalProperties false at every level; every field typed and enum/length/range-bounded; every array maxItems-capped. Integrity-keyed by intake_id + sha256. DERIVED-ONLY. OWN version pin (CORRELATION_CONTRACT_VERSION).

contract_version.description: Correlation-contract schema version. Pinned SEPARATELY on the 3.2 correlator (CORRELATION_CONTRACT_VERSION) so this record versions independently of the shared CONTRACT_VERSION and every crossing kind's pin.

intake_id.description: The intake UUIDv4 this correlation is for. The correlator writes it back onto the tracking record keyed by this.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw artifact body all lanes inspected. Integrity key, bound to intake_id; the correlator only writes onto the tracking record whose sha256 matches the combined event it correlated.

correlated_at.description: RFC3339/ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (Z-suffixed) the correlator produced this result in the Hub. The only wall-clock field (the combined event's behavioral timings stay relative).

status.description: What the invocation actually did, recorded HONESTLY (correlated / model_error / unparseable / skipped_no_signals). NOT a verdict — a 'model_error' says the call failed, never that the artifact is safe/unsafe. When status != 'correlated' the 'correlation' object is omitted (no correlation is fabricated).

status_detail.description: Optional short, bounded, non-executable note about the status (e.g. 'ThrottlingException after 5 attempts', 'response was not valid JSON'). Never raw content, never a verdict.

model_id.description: The Bedrock model id / inference-profile id invoked (RD-003, Nova Pro). Recorded for traceability + reproducibility.

attempts.description: Number of Bedrock invocation attempts made, including the final one (so the exponential-backoff retry is inspectable: 1 = succeeded first try; >1 = retried). Bounded.

latency_ms.description: Optional wall-clock duration (ms) of the successful Bedrock invocation (last attempt), for cost/perf observability. Bounded.

input_tokens.description: Optional input token count reported by Bedrock usage metadata (for cost observability). Bounded.

output_tokens.description: Optional output token count reported by Bedrock usage metadata (for cost observability). Bounded.

truncated.description: True iff the correlator capped the model's findings to MAX_FINDINGS (dropped the tail) or clipped an oversized field to fit the bounds. A completeness fact, never a verdict.

combined_complete.description: The combined event's aggregation-completeness fact (from 3.1) at the time of correlation — whether all three inputs (static / dynamic / sanitized) had landed. Carried through for traceability. An AGGREGATION-completeness fact, NEVER a verdict; the correlation may be honest over an incomplete combined event.

combined_event_contract_version.description: Version of the combined-event contract (3.1) this correlation was produced from, for traceability.

correlation.description: The Nova Pro correlation of the combined event: a bounded narrative summary + a bounded list of correlation findings (static ↔ dynamic). EVIDENCE only — NO verdict anywhere; the model was asked to correlate the evidence, never to decide. Present when status is 'correlated'; omitted when the invocation did not produce a parseable correlation (the status records why).

summary.description: The model's bounded narrative correlation of the static misconfigurations against the dynamic behavioral indicators. Inert text; never a verdict, never raw content.

highest_correlation_severity.description: The worst descriptive severity across the findings, rolled up for convenient downstream (3.3) query. Descriptive EVIDENCE, NOT a decision. Omitted when there are no findings.

finding_count.description: Number of correlation findings carried (<= MAX_FINDINGS). A bounded count.

findings.description: The bounded list of correlation findings (static ↔ dynamic). Capped at MAX_FINDINGS; a model that returns more is truncated (recorded via the top-level 'truncated' flag), never overrun. EVIDENCE only.

items.description: One correlated observation Nova Pro produced from the combined event: it ties (or fails to tie) a static misconfiguration to a dynamic behavioral indicator. Descriptive EVIDENCE for the Phase-4 human gate and the 3.3 synthesis — never a verdict. Bounded + allow-listed; the model cannot smuggle raw content or a decision through it.

kind.description: How this finding relates the two evidence lanes (correlated / static_only / dynamic_only / contradiction). Descriptive, never a verdict.

severity.description: Descriptive severity roll-up for this correlated observation — how NOTABLE it is, NOT a decision. 'unknown' when the model did not rate it.

title.description: Short, bounded, human-readable title of the correlated observation (model-produced). Inert text, never executed.

detail.description: Optional longer, bounded explanation of the correlation (model-produced). Inert text; never raw content, never a verdict.

static_refs.description: Optional bounded list of short references to the static evidence this finding draws on (e.g. a finding id / rule name surfaced in the combined event). Inert text references, never raw findings.

behavioral_refs.description: Optional bounded list of short references to the dynamic behavioral evidence this finding draws on (e.g. a syscall / event summary surfaced in the combined event). Inert text references, never the raw trace.
